unverifiedClaims: Disk, RAM, port and pruning behaviour were not researched in depth.
Windows support was not investigated.

name: ord
purpose: Index, block explorer and command-line wallet for ordinal theory (satoshi tracking and inscriptions). The explorer and JSON API are served by 'ord server'; the wallet relies on Bitcoin Core.

platforms.other: Linux x86_64 and macOS (x86_64, aarch64) archives, Homebrew, crates.io, install script.

interfaces.description: 'ord server' block explorer with JSON API enabled by default (--disable-json-api to turn it off); port chosen with --http-port.
ord index, ord server, ord wallet ... (the wallet needs ord server running since 0.16.0).
interfaces.authentication: Reads bitcoind's .cookie automatically when run by the same user with default paths, or explicit RPC credentials.

nodeCompatibility: Requires a synced bitcoind with -txindex (checked through getindexinfo); communicates over RPC; therefore not usable with a pruned node.

dependencies.notes: txindex=1, unpruned; ord wallets are Bitcoin Core descriptor wallets.

networking: Explorer on the configured HTTP port; RPC to bitcoind.
storage: Own index on top of the node (size not researched); the wallet guide mentions about 600 GB for the blockchain (undated).
security: Upstream warns that 'ord server' hosts untrusted HTML and JavaScript (cross-site scripting and spoofing risks), and that ord wallets must not hold material funds and must be kept separate from ordinary wallets because Bitcoin Core does not do sat control.
integrationMechanisms: Discovery and launching of an existing ord installation (external launcher), with the security warnings shown

feasibility.notes: Technically easy (native Windows binary, cookie authentication), but txindex, an unpruned node, untrusted web content and a wallet that can lose inscriptions make it unsuitable for default profiles.

notes: Listed for completeness as a maintained self-hosted indexer and explorer; its inclusion in the catalogue is a product decision.
unverifiedClaims: Default HTTP port of ord server, index size and RAM needs were not verified.

resources: 16 GB RAM recommended for a full sync.
security: Not reviewed in depth.
integrationMechanisms: Connect to an existing instance's API or website (research only)

name: Waterfalls
purpose: Blockstream's descriptor-based scanning server for web light-client wallets on Bitcoin and Liquid: the client sends a descriptor and receives the whole wallet history in one round trip (also a UTXO-only mode). The README says it is used at liquidwebwallet.org and benchmarks it against Esplora scans with LWK.

platforms.other: Rust; Nix build instructions in the README.

interfaces.description: Waterfalls HTTP endpoint (descriptor scan, UTXO-only mode); see docs/API.md.

name: Bitcoin RPC Proxy (btc-rpc-proxy)
purpose: Rust proxy in front of bitcoind that gives each client its own credentials with an allow-list of RPC methods (and an optional forced wallet), and performs on-demand block fetching from peers so that applications see a pruned node as unpruned.

maintenance.evidence: Last release v0.4.0 on 2024-07-13; master Cargo.toml is at 0.4.1 with the latest commit 2026-08-18 ('Bump version'), not yet released.

platforms.other: Rust, built from source; systemd socket activation on Linux; used in StartOS and the cryptoanarchy Debian repository.

interfaces.description: Bitcoin Core-compatible JSON-RPC endpoint with per-user method allow-lists and override_wallet.
interfaces.authentication: Per-user passwords in TOML configuration files.

nodeCompatibility: Sits in front of Bitcoin Core; with a pruned node it fetches pruned blocks over P2P and verifies their hash against the node.

dependencies.notes: RPC; P2P access for on-demand block fetching.

networking: Listens on a configured address; outbound to bitcoind RPC and to P2P peers for missing blocks.
resources: Low; every pruned block fetch costs bandwidth and latency.
security: Finer-grained permissions than Bitcoin Core's rpcwhitelist per application; configuration files hold passwords (permissions 600 per upstream). Does not help tools that need txindex (Fulcrum, ElectrumX, mempool) or that read REST or block files directly (electrs 0.12, Esplora electrs).
integrationMechanisms: Research: per-application RPC credentials and pruned-node block fetching for RPC-only consumers such as BTC RPC Explorer's getblock calls

feasibility.notes: No Windows builds and limited benefit: the indexers BTCortex cares about need txindex, REST or block files, which the proxy cannot emulate.

notes: Recorded under this scope as the main 'Bitcoin API gateway' found during gap analysis; may belong to another scope.
unverifiedClaims: Windows buildability and default listening port were not verified.
